findings: The locked four-frame product returned false-valid narrow-span OBW in 3/6 rectangular BPSK records.
A four-frame rectangular-FFT near-span cue separated these 30 records only by a narrow empirical margin and is not a family-wide containment proof.
A conservative 16,384-sample Hann tail-uncertainty bound rejected all 6 out-of-span BPSK records, but also withheld OBW for every tested 12 dB record in the other four families.

Increasing only the selectable span cannot recover tails that remain below the four short-frame noise floor and would also exceed the locked 64 KiB ARM persistent-memory design without a runtime redesign.

decision.reason: The promising long-observation gate lacks a separately locked multi-family/RF validation and Python-C-ARM equivalence. Promoting it now would replace a characterized limitation with an unvalidated method.
decision.ui_action: The result is named occupied bandwidth (OBW 99%) and the interface states that the approved analysis interval must contain the complete signal.

open_acceptance: Lock a new containment protocol before its evaluation set.
Measure family and SNR coverage, neighboring-emitter rejection, colored-noise behavior, memory and ARM latency.
Implement and compare Python, host C and ARM if the gate passes.
Repeat with controlled RF and a known reference emission.
